title: This Extinct Bird's Egg Was Worth More Than 100 Chicken Eggs

scenes.text: One bird's egg equaled more than one hundred chicken eggs.
The elephant bird lived on Madagascar.
It stood about ten feet tall and weighed up to a thousand pounds or more.
Its eggs were about a foot long.
Each one held about thirteen liters.
That is about seven times an ostrich egg.
Humans are thought to have wiped the birds out about a thousand years ago.
Two eggs even turned up on Australian beaches, apparently after floating four thousand miles.

description:
One bird's egg equaled more than one hundred chicken eggs.
The elephant bird of Madagascar laid eggs about a foot long, with roughly seven times the volume of an ostrich egg.
How many eggs would your omelette need?
first_comment: Bonus: some estimates say one egg equaled about 180 chicken eggs. Would you try one omelette?
